title: Reigning back-to-back champ Dodgers clinch 14th straight postseason berth
content:
CINCINNATI – The reigning back-to-back World Series champions are going back to October, as the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 14th consecutive postseason berth on Monday.

The Dodgers joined the 1991-2005 Atlanta Braves as the only teams in baseball history to make it to 14 consecutive postseasons, and clinched on their own terms. Kyle Tucker homered to open the scoring, Teoscar Hernández followed with a two-run blast of his own and Tarik Skubal delivered a gem with seven scoreless innings as the Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds, 4-1.

What felt like a fait accompli from the moment this projected $487 million roster (including payroll and luxury tax) was assembled is now set. They clinched on Sept. 14 in their 150th game after requiring 155 in 2025 and 153 in 2024. Each of those runs resulted in championships as the Dodgers have turned their self-described “golden era” into a dynasty.

This time around, they are seeking to become the first National League team ever to win three straight World Series, and the first club since the 1998-2000 New York Yankees to accomplish the feat. A fourth World Series in the last seven seasons would only burnish the club’s case for one of the most successful stretches ever for a modern club.

Another resume-builder could come as soon as Tuesday, as the Dodgers seek to clinch their 13th NL West title in that 14-year span.

Their annual long runs through October have taken their toll, as baseball’s oldest lineup by average age is showing signs of wear and tear down the stretch run. Shohei Ohtani is on the injured list for the first time as a Dodger as the organization finally shelved him after months dealing with nagging knee and biceps injuries. Freddie Freeman sat Monday for the third time in the Dodgers’ last five games as he manages tendinitis in his right knee. Andy Pages is in the early stages of a swing progression as he recuperates from a fractured left hand. Miguel Rojas reinjured his shoulder over the weekend, aggravating a torn labrum he’s played through since 2016.

They are banged up. Which makes clinching the division and staving off the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye paramount over the season’s final 12 games. They entered Monday leading Atlanta by 3 1/2 games, and trailing Milwaukee by 2 1/2 games for the NL’s top seed.

“Given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge,” manager Dave Roberts said. “So we still got to play well to finish out the season to get to that point … A lot of people could use the break.”

They have made do in spite of their injuries, in part thanks to a soft part of their schedule in September. Winning over the Reds on Monday gave the Dodgers their ninth win in their last 11 games. They have seen signs of life out of Hernández and even Tucker, who has largely disappointed in the first season of a four-year, $240 million deal he signed this winter that smashed the record for average annual value.

The club’s signing of Edwin Díaz has continued to age poorly in his first season of that deal, so much so that Roberts suggested Monday they could leave the three-time All-Star closer off the postseason roster. They added Edgardo Henriquez to their list of injured players on Monday, removing the club’s best reliever over the last month from the picture. Ohtani, Freeman, Pages, Rojas and others will still be playing through aches and pains by the time October rolls around.

“I think right now it’s front of mind, it’s not great,” Roberts said. “But I will say this: Once you get to October, athletes have a magical way of feeling better. It happens every single year, where there’s that extra adrenaline that athletes get when you get to the postseason.”

They still boast what is likely baseball’s most talented roster and an established track record of postseason success that might be enough to make history.

This story will be updated.
